date_basis: Primary Dagstuhl publication metadata dated 5 October 2026, checked 13 October 2026.
summary: AIDev-based comparisons of 669 developer-repository pairs in agent-exposed repositories with 228 control pairs find increased PR-description length and small test-change associations. Apparent review changes in before/after comparisons do not remain significant after comparison with controls. This challenges simple attribution of every review trend to agents, without establishing better delivered software.
limitations: Nonrandom adoption defined by first visible agent PR, not first AI use; selection of persistent contributors and active reviewers, median-split controls and limited matching weaken causal identification. Description length and test-file heuristics do not measure explanation quality or defect prevention. Null review contrasts do not establish equivalence. Reporting questions in the time-window and misattribution summaries are logged for clarification; no replication was run.

date_basis: Microsoft Research identifies Joule April 2026; Crossref issue date is August 2026. Distinct online/issue timing retained without inventing an exact day.
summary: Models optimized production-scale inference and efficiency pathways. Short-query energy can be substantially lower than poorly matched estimates, while long reasoning and agentic workloads increase demand. Per-query efficiency does not determine aggregate resource use.
limitations: Microsoft-affiliated authors. Read public institutional abstract and related author repository description, not full journal text. Assumption-dependent modeled inference, not universal metering, marginal carbon or a full lifecycle assessment. Efficiency opportunities are not guaranteed reductions in total demand.
verification_scope: Official Microsoft Research title, eight authors and journal/DOI link crosschecked with Crossref metadata; public abstract and authors' Zenodo scope caveats read. Publisher full text returned 403; June repository version not presumed identical to the journal article.

title: Disruption without dividend? - How the digital divide and task differences split GenAI's global impact
authors: Gmyrek, Paweł; Viollaz, Mariana; Winkler, Hernan

limitations: Potential exposure and infrastructure constraints, not observed job displacement, adoption or realized productivity. Read the institutional abstract and detailed findings, not the complete paper or reproducibility package. ILO and World Bank versions describe one study family, not independent replications.
verification_scope: ILO author/date/DOI and detailed findings inspected; World Bank reproducibility catalog identity checked. Publication, news and package dates distinguished; underlying exposure calculations not rerun.

verification_scope: Byline/date and public sections on comparison boundaries, output lengths and hidden agent calls inspected; primary study separately identified. No independent energy measurements performed.
